cases.label: correct
cases.question: In NYC, how high above the floor may the top of a wall-mounted hand-held extinguisher be if its gross weight is 45 pounds?
cases.expectedAnswer: At most 3.5 feet for hand-held extinguisher exceeding 40 pounds. Bottom floor clearance at least 4 inches if addressed.
cases.answerText: **3.5 feet (42 inches / 1,067 mm) maximum above the floor.** The 2022 NYC Fire Code sets that limit for a hand-held portable extinguisher with a gross weight exceeding 40 pounds; at 45 pounds, this extinguisher falls within that rule (FC § 906.9.2).

citationDetails.codeEdition: 2022 NYC Fire Code — current consolidated text

cases.operativeRuleReview: The cited 2022 FC 906 excerpt includes complete 906.9.2: a hand-held extinguisher exceeding 40 lb has a top-height limit of 3.5 ft. The answer correctly applies the 45 lb premise and gives the equivalent 42 in/1067 mm. Bottom clearance is an independent unasked condition; no whole-installation approval is implied.

cases.label: correct
cases.question: If we replace it with one weighing exactly 40 pounds, does the top-height limit become 5 feet?
cases.expectedAnswer: Yes. Gross weight not exceeding 40 pounds has top limit 5 feet; bottom floor clearance still at least 4 inches.
cases.answerText: **Yes.** If the replacement hand-held extinguisher’s gross weight is exactly 40 pounds, its top may be no more than 5 feet above the floor: the 5-foot rule covers extinguishers weighing 40 pounds or less. The 3.5-foot limit applies only when gross weight exceeds 40 pounds (FC §§ 906.9.1–906.9.2).

cases.question: In NYC, may the fire watch leave as soon as ordinary indoor welding ends? I am asking about the minimum post-work watch, not the rest of the permit requirements.
cases.expectedAnswer: No. Fire watch required during hot work and continues at least 30 minutes after conclusion; duration may be extended by commissioner/responsible hot-work-program person.
cases.answerText: **No.** For hot work, the fire watch must continue for **at least 30 minutes after the work ends**. The commissioner or the person responsible for implementing the hot-work program may extend it based on the hazards or work performed (2022 NYC Fire Code § 3504.2.1).

cases.question: For two adjoining NYC C4-2 buildings on the same block, can their required loading berths be supplied by one shared facility if it has enough berths for the combined floor area, direct access to both buildings, and a compliant design?

cases.answerText:
**Yes, under ZR § 36-65:** required loading berths may be provided in one joint facility for adjoining buildings within a single block if the facility has at least the number required for their combined floor area, provides direct access to each building, and its design and layout meet the adequacy standards set by the Commissioner of Buildings. But ZR § 144-53 separately states that loading berths are not required in any district, although they are permitted. It also says that any berths provided are deemed required for determining the amount of floor area in a building. The supplied provisions state these rules without resolving their relationship. The supplied text identifies C4 districts, including C4-2, for this joint-berth provision. Your stated facts address those conditions, assuming “compliant design” means compliance with those standards.

The required count is determined under ZR § 36-62; the supplied table places C4-2 among the listed districts, but the excerpt does not provide enough table structure to independently verify a specific count. ZR § 144-53 separately states that loading berths are not required in any district, although they are permitted; any berths provided are deemed required for determining the amount of floor area in a building.
